get.description: Gets a list of Events for the given Project ID

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: If specified, only events with a date time equal to or after the specified date time will be returned. Valid date formats 'YYYY-MM-DD', 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss', or 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sss'. ISO-8601 date format without time zone.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: If specified, only events with a date time equal or prior to the specified date time will be returned. Valid date formats 'YYYY-MM-DD', 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss', or 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sss'. ISO-8601 date format without time zone.

Problem-Detail.description: The Problem Detail format defines a way to carry machine-readable details of errors in a HTTP response to avoid the need to define new error response formats for HTTP APIs. Problem details can be extended and defined for specific problem types.

type.description:
An absolute URI that identifies the problem type.  When
dereferenced, it should provide human-readable documentation
for the problem type (e.g., using HTML).

title.description:
A short, human-readable summary of the problem type. It should
not change from occurrence to occurrence of the problem.

status.description:
The HTTP status code generated by the origin server for this
occurrence of the problem.

detail.description:
A human readable explanation specific to this occurrence of the
problem.

instance.description:
A URI reference that identifies the specific occurrence of
the problem.  It may or may not yield further information
if dereferenced.

401-GENERIC-RESPONSE.description: Response when the user does not supply valid authorization credentials.

example.title: Unauthorized
example.detail: Not authorized to perform this action.

404-GENERIC-RESPONSE.description:
Response when the resource does not exist or the user does not have rights
to the resource.

example.title: Not Found
example.detail: The requested resource was not found.

409-GENERIC-RESPONSE.description: Response when the request could not be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the target resource.

400-GENERIC-RESPONSE.description: Response for when a bad request is provided.

Location.description:
The "Location" header field is used in some responses to refer to a
specific resource in relation to the response.  The type of
relationship is defined by the combination of request method and
status code semantics.
Reference: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-7.1.2
